 "iterations": [

   "theme": "Analysis of Dinamo's defeat at Poljud: poor lineup, coach Kovačević, transfer window and refereeing",
   "sections": [
    {
     "subtitle": "Derby from the Edge of the European Union: a podcast recorded from England",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis and Profa in a hotel room in England, with a conversation about the trip and the match at the stadium",
     "content": "The episode of the 8_24 podcast begins in unusual circumstances. Profa admits in the introduction that it is not easy to record outside the European Union, and it is even harder after a defeat in the derby. He adds that the result from Poljud hit them seriously, although they spent nice days in England.\n\nDenis explains why they are watching Dinamo's derby from a hotel room, and not from Poljud or from the studio. According to his words, they had an opportunity that comes once in a lifetime, maybe more than once, to be guests of their former coach. Therefore they accepted it with both hands.\n\nDenis describes what they have already managed to see in England:\n\n- the match of Hull and Everton, with a note that the locals corrected them about the pronunciation of the club's name,\n- a training session that reminded him of a day \"from a fairy tale\",\n- the match of Manchester and Tottenham on the day of recording,\n- the derby of Dinamo and Hajduk, which they watched in the hotel before that.\n\nProfa asks jokingly whether the match at the \"Theatre of Dreams\" eased the pain of the defeat. Denis answers that the match was not especially good quality. Still, the whole atmosphere of English football delighted him. He says he saw why people praise the English atmosphere so much. In the second half he mentions a red card and two goals. He thinks viewers will still be more interested in talking about Dinamo.\n\nProfa then greets friends Tonči and Luka and thanks them for the greeting at the end of their video. He adds that, thanks to a combination of work and a visit in England, they temporarily \"made themselves English\".",

    {
     "subtitle": "A Hundred Alibis, and None Holds: Denis Does Not Look for Excuses",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis explains that Hajduk deserved to win and that Dinamo was poorly set up",
     "content": "Profa introduces the topic with a story about Kobe Bryant's interview after a lost final. The basketball player then said he could find a hundred alibis, but that he would not use any. Profa then lists Dinamo's possible excuses: Mišić was not there, Stojković was not fully healthy, the pitch was bad, and Hajduk very probably should have remained with a player fewer. He asks Denis whether any of that consoles him and whether it is an alibi.\n\nDenis answers briefly: **he would have no alibis**. He thinks Hajduk was better and deserved to win. The refereeing and disputed situations will be a subject of discussion, but he does not see them as the cause of the defeat. According to him, the cause is Dinamo's poor play and generally poor setup, and especially a problematic starting lineup.\n\nIn this vivid way he describes what he would do if he were Dinamo's coach or director:\n\n- he would print on the nicest printer pictures of all eleven Hajduk players and hang them in the dressing room,\n- he would tell the players that they were not just beaten, but beaten up and outplayed,\n- he would frame Bamba's picture and put it in front of the whole defence, with a message that he dominated against them.\n\nDenis stresses that the most devastating thing is that Dinamo, according to his assessment, has 10 or 10 and a half better players than Hajduk's 11. He judges that Dinamo's squad on paper is twice as good. Despite that, Hajduk won without a \"bunker\" and without a lucky deflection. Dinamo played a good part of the match in a low or mid block and did not show anything that is expected of it.",
     "keywords": [

    {
     "subtitle": "Divorce Without a Culprit: Dinamo Needs Shock Therapy",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis compares the relationship between the coach and the club to a couple whose love has disappeared",
     "content": "Denis thinks the derby result is part of a worrying run. He lists the big matches that Dinamo lost this year: Osijek and Viking, with a note that Dinamo has \"luckily\" kept the match with Rijeka, which it has not yet played. In the conversation Profa recalls that Dinamo has achieved only three wins in the last nine matches.\n\nDenis explains the problem with a comparison to family friends, a married couple who divorced. He says they are great people, but the energy and love were lost. Although individually excellent, together they could no longer go on. He sees the same in Dinamo: love and energy can be born again, but the current situation with the coaching staff and the squad is not compatible with the club's expectations and its goals.\n\nDenis concludes that the team needs **shock therapy**. He wonders whether it can pull it out of itself before Anderlecht. He emphasizes that the people may still be good, but not necessarily together. He thinks this is the \"last chance\" and questions the sense of insisting on what does not work from match to match.",
     "keywords": [
      "run of defeats",
      "shock therapy",
      "energy in the club",
      "Anderlecht",
      "coaching staff"
     ],

    {
     "subtitle": "Three Figures That Did Not Click: Kovačević and Stojković's Readiness",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis analyzes Kovačević's substitutions in the 60th minute and Stojković's role",
     "content": "Denis says that coach Kovačević in the derby \"took responsibility into his own hands\". He decided to make three substitutions in the 60th minute, whereby, according to Denis, he himself showed that he missed with everything he had conceived for the match.\n\nAbout Stojković, Denis does not want to speak of a miss. He recalls that the player himself said that on Friday he had only started to train, so realistically he was not ready. Profa notes that on Tuesday he was a star, but Denis holds to what Kovačević said in Cres and believes that it is true. If the player really trained only from Friday, there would not be too many reasons for him to play, let alone on a soft, muddy pitch. Denis would not have brought him in, because the match was without rhythm.\n\nProfa also mentions that quite a few people reproached Stojković's coming on against Vukovar. Denis adds that not even there would he risk it, given the pitch. If the player is completely healthy, says Profa, then he should not be spared. Denis admits that this did not have too much logic for him. Maybe the coach wanted to give the player rhythm.\n\nDenis concludes that what Dinamo plays looks like nothing. He emphasizes that the match against Anderlecht practically decides: if Dinamo does not win, it will be almost at the exit door of the Europa League.",
     "keywords": [
      "Kovačević",

    {
     "subtitle": "Downward Trajectory: European Exams Kovačević Did Not Pass",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis lists European failures from last season to Hapoel and Viking",
     "content": "Denis admits that Kovačević as Dinamo's coach achieved a good result. However, he claims that precisely where Dinamo needed to make a breakthrough, in Europe, he failed every exam. He starts from last season. Dinamo then entered among the 24 teams in the Europa League, but Denis warns that even that cannot be fairly defended. He mentions the match in Belgium, in which Dinamo could have gone through, and a very bad match in Zagreb. This season in Europe he already sees a failure that has been made and that can be even bigger if Dinamo does not enter among the 24 teams, which does not seem at all certain to him.\n\nProfa throws in the argument that Kovačević can defend himself by the fact that the club openly communicated that the Europa League is the goal. But Profa notes that, because of last year's success, Dinamo was considered a favourite and had a nice path towards the Champions League. Denis responds that the trend is downward. Against Tun, Dinamo went through on God's luck, with a red card and a reversed situation, and in neither of the two matches was it better than a very modest team. Against Viking it was bad. The match with Hapoel Denis describes as the luckiest for Kovačević in the whole tenure, regardless of the heavy defeats against Celta and Lille.\n\nProfa recalls that Dinamo had a heavy \"big slap\" from Osijek, then a catastrophic level of play against Hapoel and harder wins against Lokomotiva, partly because of red cards. He judges that people were not so angry only because of the three-week break between matches. Denis adds that against Hapoel Dinamo did not look like a team that has some justification, because each of them dominated, and yet it looked bad.",

      "Europa League",
      "downward trend",
      "European failure",

    {
     "subtitle": "Bad Energy Springs from the Top: Transfer Window, Management and Zvonimir Boban",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis criticizes the transfer window and the moves of Dinamo's management",
     "content": "Profa asks how much the first team and the play were actually rehearsed. Denis thinks it is logical to rehearse for about ten days and that for a week the idea with which one is going must be known. He does not understand how Galešić plays alongside Dominguez and why other players, who in his opinion deserved a chance, do not take part. As an example he cites a lad who is perhaps the best defensive player this season, and does not get a chance. He stresses that there are more examples of players toward whom the club has sinned.\n\nAs the worst thing in Dinamo this season Denis cites bad energy. He thinks it is caused by bad moves inside the club. He judges that the **transfer window was done catastrophically**. He says that a person with power, contacts and resources like Zvonimir Boban cannot afford such a transfer window in crucial positions. He also reproaches the bringing in of „almost all clumsy players”, the not bringing in of a goalkeeper and the not giving of a chance, which are already old topics.\n\nDenis connects this with Boban's position. Boban, in his opinion, got into some kind of \"mad masochism\" around the stadium. He thinks it naive to expect that a tangle of negative energy, not only around the coach but around the entire management, will not be reflected on the team. Last year Kovačević had behind him the stable figure of Zvonimir Boban and maximum authority in carrying out decisions. Today neither players nor fans are firmly behind him, so Kovačević no longer swims as before. Denis warns that players are \"the most popular commodity in the world\".\n\nThe opening part of the season can still serve as an excuse, but not forever. Denis repeats that he sees no sense in avoiding big cuts. He also stresses that, with Hajduk and Rijeka like this, Dinamo would have to be champion for the question to be closed at all.",
     "keywords": [
      "transfer window",
      "Zvonimir Boban",
      "bad energy",
      "club management",
      "big cuts"
     ],

    {
     "subtitle": "Europe Is Not a Luxury: The Club's Budget Depends on Success on the Continent",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis explains why Europe is a priority and the foundation of Dinamo's budget",
     "content": "Profa asks whether Denis is worried about the title or about Europe, noting that the title is for now not the main concern. Denis answers that he does not know where the idea comes from that Europe is not the most important pillar of the club's long-term stability. According to him, Europe is the priority both last year and this year. A Dinamo that will not play the Europa League has achieved the minimum of minimums, but it needs to play, and successfully.\n\nHe explains the link between European success and finances:\n\n- if Dinamo does not play successfully in Europe, there are no player sales,\n- without sales nobody can fulfil the budget,\n- the long-term strategy must include giving a chance to young people, and then foreigners should not be the only solution either.\n\nDenis adds that it is precisely that way that the club, with a lot of money \"thrown to the wind\", burned the bridge towards the future. If the strategy is long-term, he says, then nobody would have anything to reproach it for.",
     "keywords": [
      "Europa League",
      "club budget",
      "player sales",
      "long-term strategy",

      "Dinamo",
      "Europa League"

    {
     "subtitle": "Hajduk's First Goal and the Lack of a Plan B Without Mišić",
     "screenshot_description": "Analysis of Hajduk's first goal and a conversation about play without Mišić",
     "content": "The conversation then returns to the derby itself and Hajduk's first goal. Denis describes it as a combination of circumstances. Maračić made a block on one Dinamo player, which according to Denis was certainly a tactical idea of aggressiveness at that set piece, and for that he gives him every credit. The ball then passed to the Hajduk player who shot from that angle and, according to Denis's words, did not even see the ball at all. Denis calls this an unlucky circumstance. Profa notes that Šimun Hrgović's ball that preceded the situation was excellent.\n\nDenis calls the absence of Josip Mišić an already told story. He says Dinamo without him looks boring, and on paper has not managed to win a single match in which it could not use what he gives it. He thinks one could have gone with another formation, especially in Split, in unusual circumstances and without Stojković and Mišić. Insisting on the same postulates as when all the settings are different, he says, is **football suicide**. He sees no sense in Dinamo functioning all the time in a 4-3-3 system, while not trying to surprise with anything.\n\nProfa agrees and describes how Dinamo tried to replace Mišić. There was no attempt at opening the play through the middle, rather they were mostly long balls from the back line. He does not blame an individual, but the organization of play, because no attempt at all was made to replace Mišić. Denis concludes: Dinamo made a copy of Mišić instead of making a new model for the situation in which he is absent.",
     "keywords": [
      "Hajduk's first goal",
      "Mišić",
      "plan B",
      "formation",
      "organization of play"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Hajduk",
      "Maračić",
      "Šimun Hrgović",
      "Josip Mišić",
      "Stojković",
      "Split",
      "Dinamo"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Missed Preparation and the Question of the Right Back",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis and Profa discuss the starting lineup and the player at right back",
     "content": "Profa asks Denis whether, when he saw the lineup, he expected 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3 and admits that he himself thought it would be 4-2-3-1. Denis answers that this would have been a more desirable change than what was seen. His assessment is: **missed lineup, missed match preparation** and Garcia took the win in everything. He adds that it is not difficult to prepare for Dinamo, because everyone knows what and how it will play. If Dinamo is not markedly dominant or energetically good, it is no advantage even against Lokomotiva, and all coaches know how to play against it.\n\nProfa also talks about Bamba. He notes that he is not Dinamo's biggest problem and that everything he did he did via the side on which he played. But he thinks his movements in attack were also deficient.\n\nMost of the discussion is about the right back. Profa stresses that the coach's stubbornness bothers him when it comes to that player and mentions how the coach justified the decision after the match. He additionally emphasized that he will not play with three centre-backs, although Galešić has several times played as a \"third centre-back\", that is, right back.\n\nDenis has not won the league as a coach nor does he have a licence, but he thinks he can judge that **Tadinac in quality does not match Dinamo's team and demands**, especially in big matches. He stresses that he is a player for situations when the opponent defends in a low block and when his explosiveness and occasional good cross can come to the fore. He is not a young player and has no sales potential. He also reasons that, if Dinamo cannot produce a right back, then it can shut down the school. Of Galešić he says that he proved he can play in that position, and yet does not get a chance. Because of this he sees only two possible explanations: the decision was imposed on the coach or the coach is \"lost\". A third scenario, according to him, does not exist.\n\nProfa notes that Tadinac looked fine against Lokomotiva, and Denis responds that scouting is what worries him. It surprises him even more that the player ends up in the starting lineup in important matches.",
     "keywords": [
      "starting lineup",
      "match preparation",
      "right back",
      "Galešić",
      "scouting"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Garcia",
      "Bamba",
      "Tadinac",
      "Galešić",

      "Dinamo",
      "Kovačević"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Dominguez's Credit and the Coach Who Leads Scouts",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis criticizes Dominguez's status and the coach's lack of self-criticism",
     "content": "The conversation then moves to the centre-back pair and Hajduk's equalizing goal, which came after a foul. Profa and Denis judge that both Dominguez and the other centre-back played bad matches. Profa recalls that, in his opinion, the coach after the match practically admitted everything that is wrong, including the changes.\n\nDenis does not understand on what basis Dominguez has such credit. Dinamo has perhaps the greatest breadth in quality precisely in the centre-back positions, with Galešić and Radeljić, that is, four very good centre-backs. Dominguez, according to him, made over ten direct errors in important matches at a high level. Despite that he still has \"crazy credit\" with Kovačević. Denis describes this as believing in the wrong players.\n\nHe particularly misses the **self-criticism** of Dinamo's coach after the match and towards the players. All of that, he says, seems as if he leads scouts: after the match comes the message that next weekend it will be better. „Dinamo can't do that”, he concludes.\n\nProfa also mentions Kovačević's statement that he cannot reproach the players for anything. He adds that the coach said he would go mad if he once heard that, but he is not sure whether he said it immediately after the match.",
     "keywords": [
      "Dominguez",
      "centre-backs",
      "self-criticism",

      "Dinamo"
     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Praise for Hajduk: A Good Match Without a Bunker",
     "screenshot_description": "Profa reads a greeting from viewer Ana Lovrić and comments on Hajduk's play",
     "content": "In the middle of the conversation Denis warns Profa that a message from viewer Ana Lovrić has arrived. Profa answers her with a greeting and reads her comment: she wants to praise her Hajduk, which after so many years did not defend itself and did not stand in a block against Dinamo.\n\nDenis agrees with the content of the message and judges that Hajduk played a good match. He describes the first half as even. He admits that Hajduk was slightly better to him and with greater initiative, but agrees that it was 50:50. In the second half, after the initial minutes while regular conditions still prevailed, Hajduk was, according to him, much better. He adds that Dinamo did not show desire in the fight for second balls and that Hajduk's players \"beat them up\".\n\nProfa praises Hajduk's positioning in the middle of the pitch, because of which its players always looked closer to the ball, and mentions that Luka spoke well about second balls. He stresses that he does not want to underestimate Hajduk, but when he sees those players, he does not want to even remember them, regardless of the number of foreigners and of the fact that they once mocked Dinamo. He adds that this season Hajduk's results have been changeable: Hajduk lost at Rujevica to Rijeka 1:0, and coach Garcia to this day has not won a single derby.\n\nDenis says that Bamba was not just good, but dominated, and Profa defends him to some extent. He describes him as a player who, when he looks good, looks super, and when he does not look good, then he does not look good. Denis perceives him as a player without technique. Profa notes that Hajduk's Krakow is last in the league, and Denis concludes that Dinamo should not respect so much either Hajduk's numbers or its team.",
     "keywords": [
      "Hajduk's play",
      "second balls",
      "Bamba",
      "positioning",
      "Garcia"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Ana Lovrić",

    {
     "subtitle": "Criticism Without Personal Attacks and the Mystery of the Wingers in 4-3-3",
     "screenshot_description": "Profa and Denis discuss the role of the wingers in the 4-3-3 system",
     "content": "Denis warns that reactions to a defeat must be balanced towards the players and the coach. He agrees that one must not attack on a personal level. He criticizes social networks, on which, he says, more and more criticism relates to non-football reasons, to the coach, the president and others. Such criticism becomes meaningless and moves away from what happens on the pitch. He adds that before some matches a curtain was noticed that protected people in the club, which is now too weak.\n\nProfa then opens the topic of the 4-3-3 system. He recalls that it maximizes the chance for the wingers and asks what the wingers did in the derby. Denis answers: nothing. As a big mistake he cites that the engine of the play does not enter the corridor, and even in secondary roles the players did not show the tactical knowledge that would be expected.\n\nDenis presents how he would put the team together. In the eight position **Ivan Sušec** would play instead of Zajec. On the left he would go with his own choice, and he would give a chance to Hodžić. On the right side Franjo Topić or Alen would play.\n\nProfa mentions a viewer's comment that Ivanišević and Almeida both like to come into the centre and so do not give width. Denis rejects this: he has never heard that a left winger cannot play on the right or vice versa, and calls it the greatest stupidity he has heard in modern football analysis. He also mentions that Ivanišević was brought in as an eight, and today was one of the more dangerous in attack, although Denis in the end agreed that he did not play in that position.",
     "keywords": [
      "4-3-3 system",
      "wingers",
      "social networks",
      "criticism of the coach",
      "Sušec"
     ],
     "entities": [
      "Ivan Sušec",

    {
     "subtitle": "Zajec's Drop in Form and Praise for Individuals",
     "screenshot_description": "Profa asks Denis about Niko Zajec's drop, and Denis praises Belje",
     "content": "Profa asks Denis how he views Niko Zajec's drastic drop this season. Denis says he does not know what exactly is wrong, but recalls that last season Zajec was, along with Stojković, the best footballer in the league. If an MVP award were handed out, he sees both names among the main candidates.\n\nThen he praises Belje, whom he describes as a positive surprise. What he did last season he continues this season too, and Denis sees that he is ready to do it continuously. He states that last season he scored over 20 goals in the HNL, and compares him with Duje Čop, who once scored over 20 goals, but is not a player who can repeat that from season to season. About Belje he says he deserves every credit and that today he would not reproach him for anything in particular.\n\nProfa agrees that Belje was by far Dinamo's best player and adds praise, although he had problems with digestion. He also mentions that one goal was the result of a big error, but Denis does not consider it decisive. Profa repeats that Hajduk's first goal seemed funny to him.",

      "Zajec",
      "drop in form",

    {
     "subtitle": "What Is 4-3-3 For in Dinamo? Salaries, Money and the Question of Sense",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis asks whether it makes sense for Dinamo to play 4-3-3 and talks about thrown-away money",
     "content": "Denis stresses a question that, as he says, has been nagging him for all five months. It is asked by „many people” who are coaches: is there any football logic for a team like Dinamo to play 4-3-3 with the first team, like the best teams in the history of football, among which he mentions Barcelona. He claims that he has not heard anyone say that it makes sense.\n\nHe explains when this system would make sense: when Dinamo would not have to be a club chasing the champion's title. Then, he says, a club like Istra would do it, for which it is all the same whether it will be third or eighth, and the main goal is for players from the juniors to move easily into the seniors and to be sold. Such a system helps sales, because it is easier to sell players who play 4-3-3 and to buy players for that system. But Dinamo has other goals: to be good in Europe, to win the title and in that way to fill the budget.\n\nHere Denis also mentions thrown-away money. He finds it unbelievable how much money has been thrown to the wind, and at the same time stresses that the lost derby shows that Dinamo is not better even when the players have experience.\n\nDenis also poses a question to the players. Their names and salaries should be studied before they say whether they are what Dinamo needs. He asks whether players like Mišić could play constantly in that system or should have raised their voice, and given the coach more freedom to try something else, especially in derbies and European matches.",
     "keywords": [
      "4-3-3 system",
      "club budget",
      "players' salaries",
      "Barcelona",
      "tactical variety"
     ],
     "entities": [

     ]
    },
    {
     "subtitle": "Rain as an Alibi and the Psychology of the Derby",
     "screenshot_description": "Denis and Profa talk about the irregular conditions at Poljud",
     "content": "Denis ironizes one of the alibis, the rain and the pitch. He stresses that, while the pitch was in an almost water-polo state, Hajduk's players looked much better, but Dinamo created the most danger precisely then. He says: \"We created the most danger while there were irregular conditions.\"\n\nProfa adds that psychologically Hajduk was also better because Dinamo withdrew. Denis thinks the missed chance was big because a goal at that moment, in his assessment, would have extinguished Hajduk for the whole season. Profa follows up that then, if Dinamo had scored, Dinamo's player would still be „Mister Derby”.\n\nDenis links this with the general problem with people who praise or condemn according to current form. He thinks that a tendency of bad results gives birth to criticism that crosses the line, and when \"everyone is booting him\", there is nothing special to say.
